featured.title: US–Iran Conflict Keeps Global Markets on Alert
featured.content: The latest exchange of military strikes between the United States and Iran has increased concerns about a wider regional conflict and possible disruption to energy supplies. Oil prices remain elevated as investors monitor developments around the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: BREAKING: US–Iran Conflict Remains Highly Volatile
articles.description: Renewed military exchanges between the United States and Iran are keeping the Middle East on high alert. The conflict is also raising concerns about shipping, energy supplies and the possibility of a wider regional escalation.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains Critical to Global Energy Security
articles.description: The conflict continues to create uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important energy routes. Reduced shipping activity is increasing concern about possible supply disruptions and higher energy costs.

articles.title: Nepal Flood Disaster Leaves More Than 1,200 Dead
articles.description: Rescue teams in Nepal are continuing a major search operation after catastrophic flooding caused by a glacial collapse. Reuters reports that more than 1,200 people have died and thousands remain missing, while teams search for survivors trapped in hydropower tunnels.

articles.title: Rescuers Search for Workers Trapped in Nepal Tunnels
articles.description: Authorities are concentrating rescue efforts around hydropower projects where workers may still be alive inside tunnel chambers. International teams from several countries are assisting with the search.

articles.title: Global Economy Watches Middle East Conflict Closely
articles.description: Higher oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty are creating new concerns for inflation, interest rates and economic growth as governments and financial markets assess the consequences of the US–Iran confrontation.

articles.title: Trump Signs Bill to Avert US Government Shutdown
articles.description: President Donald Trump has signed a temporary funding bill that keeps US federal agencies operating beyond October 1. The measure extends government funding through December 11 while Congress works on full-year spending legislation.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: Conflict, energy markets and humanitarian emergencies dominate Thursday's global picture. The US–Iran confrontation remains highly volatile and continues to create uncertainty around Middle East security and global energy supplies. Brent crude remains close to $95 a barrel. Nepal is facing a devastating humanitarian crisis after catastrophic flooding, with more than 1,200 deaths reported and thousands still missing. In the United States, President Donald Trump has signed a temporary funding bill to prevent a government shutdown through December 11, although the country's debt remains above $40 trillion. Canada has kept its interest rate at 2.25%, while the Japanese yen has strengthened sharply. Migration tensions continue in Ceuta, and AI regulation is increasingly becoming a political issue.

bigQuestion: When international tensions threaten the global economy, should governments prioritise diplomacy even when negotiations require difficult compromises?
